the role of the Fermitin family of proteins in cardiac syncytial development.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Fermitin proteins (Fit1 and Fit2) regulate the development of a functioning cardiac syncytium and are required for normal cardiomyocyte adhesion in Drosophilamelanogaster.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Drosophila Fermitins regulate the development of a cardiac syncytium.

The main takeaway from our work is that
we have shown that Fermitins, the Drosophila Kindlins, are required for the development of the heart in Drosophia.
the two Drosophilia Fermitins, FIt1 and FIt2 can functionally compensate each other to control the development of a syncytial cardiac muscle in flies.
